title: A herb stand where a third of the plants grow by their own rule
question: Both are herb. One is the stand you have now, one has real variation in it. Does the varied one still read as a single species -- or as a mess?
context_md:
Plants inherit their growth program and it can mutate. **At the rate that ships today the mutation never reaches a plant** -- measured: 60,000 frames of herb at the shipped rate produces a stand *identical in every number* to the same world with mutation switched off. 45 mutations fired, and none of the 28 plants that carried one ever grew past a seedling.

This is what raising that rate 30x looks like. Same world, same seed, same frame (noon, 21,600), everything else equal.

What I already checked, so you don't have to look for it: the varied stand is **not** sicker. Same number of seeds set (1,788 against 1,789), plants slightly *larger* on average, and across four world seeds establishment moves +3%, +4%, +6%, -13% -- no consistent cost. Even mutating *every single birth* does not break the stand.

So the question is purely a look-and-feel one, and it is the one thing I could not measure: **is a species with a visible minority of odd individuals in it better than a species where every plant is the same plant?** If it reads as broken, or as noise rather than as variation, that is the answer and I will take the rate back down.
